items.label: A
items.critique: 'Gahhhhhh! No! Don't kill me!' slapstick, a half-blind hermit, 'Oh....' with four dots and a scroll 'about bats' as the reward. This is Westwood's gag and plainness, with a vague hint in the reminder.

items.label: B
items.critique: A father's horn as an heirloom, bandits mocking the town, 'I'll pay you from my own pocket' and a yes/no close. The reward of 80 gold plus boots and the detailed journal line mark the template.

items.label: C
items.critique: A monk who calls the player 'my son' and drops his mother's beads, with the crypt door 'behind the altar'. It is tidy and warm, but the mother's-heirloom hook and the gold-plus-item reward match its siblings.

items.label: D
items.critique: A grandfather's lantern 'for sixty years', a tavern named for it, Urchins 'south of the ford' and 60 gold, a potion and free ale. Over-specified, with exclamations everywhere.

items.label: E
items.critique: Exposition-heavy plot handoff: a secret route behind bookcases, 'Unsavory elements dwell in the shadows!' and a curt 'we have no time for mourning'. A masking slip ('[Person]' cottage') and plot glue feel original.

items.label: F
items.critique: Mayor's welcome, a scepter stolen by urchins who 'have gone mad', and 'nettlesome urchins' as a reminder that gives no direction. It hands off to the Captain and a shop, which is campaign structure.

items.label: G
items.critique: A father's tinderbox 'for forty years', its location repeated in the offer, reminder and journal, and 60 gold plus a potion with a joke. It is the same mould as B/D/I.

items.label: H
items.critique: A short, slightly stilted plea ('he'll be destroyed', 'kind sir', 'Could you... would you') and a generic 'token of my appreciation' with no amount. It is weak, but its weakness is Westwood's.

items.label: I
items.critique: 'Dearie', egg money and 'Ugh, it's slimy... but it's mine!' are funny and plain. The mother's ring, exact 30 gold, a potion and a geographic journal follow the formula.

items.label: J
items.critique: 'I am thankful you are here at last, for we are in dire need', 'foul demoness' and 'sooner than you think' are the main plot's formal register. The journal is a bare 'Retrieve the [Thing].'

tells: New heirloom quests always use a family heirloom with a duration ('my father's... for forty years', 'my mother's... all her life', 'sixty years'). Westwood's stolen items are functional or plot objects (spectacles, scepter, an artifact).

New rewards are exact gold plus an item plus a joke ('Take 60 gold and this potion. You'll need it...'). Westwood gives '500 in gold', 'a token of my appreciation', a scroll or spells, often without a number.
New reminders repeat the exact location. Westwood's reminders are often unhelpful or atmospheric ('Those nettlesome urchins...').
New journal entries name person, item and place with directions. Westwood's are short ('Retrieve the [Thing].').
Westwood's quest-givers move the plot on (go see the Captain, buy supplies, a teleporter). The new givers close the quest locally with a cheer.
